segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I kept 2200 as my working target. I nudged it a little in my head, but I didn't sit down and recalculate from the new numbers.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant retained the handed-off 2200 target and made only a small adjustment despite learning the actual count and cycle conditions had changed. This is the primary manifestation of the single planned anchoring instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I could've recalculated from scratch ... Or radioed the hump conductor ... I didn't do either right away — I just carried the number forward.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a separate articulation of the same estimate-revision decision: the participant identifies recalculation and consultation as alternatives but carries the initial target forward. It is not an additional planned occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Probably if the discrepancy had been bigger ... if it'd been 50 cars ... Three extra cars didn't feel like enough to abandon the plan.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant describes a threshold for abandoning the initial target and treats the actual discrepancy as insufficient to do so. This is a repeated manifestation of the same planned anchoring instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We'd had a derailment at this yard about three weeks earlier ... and that was fresh in my mind. I made the call to pull the whole eleven-car cut.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The recent derailment is explicitly connected to the choice to pull the full cut after a borderline alert. This is an initial articulation of the single planned availability-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The derailment three weeks back was still sitting with me ... I didn't want a repeat, so I went bigger than the book probably called for.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The vivid recent event drives a response beyond standard procedure for the borderline reading. This repeats the same planned availability-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It didn't carry the same weight as the derailment ... even though logically the wet-weather false positives happen a lot more often.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says the recalled derailment outweighed the more frequent wet-weather false positives. This is the clearest articulation of the planned availability-bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: One found a hairline mark ... The other inspected independently and cleared it ... There was also an old repair entry ... I ended up treating it as still suspect and asked for a third pass.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant describes treating the car as suspect after receiving both a mark and an independent clearance, while also mentioning the old repair entry. This is an initial articulation of the single planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I leaned toward Carman A's finding ... Between the mark and that history, it felt like enough to keep the car flagged. I asked for a third inspection rather than accepting Carman B's clearance.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant favors evidence supporting suspicion and rejects the independent clearance, using the old unrelated repair entry as supporting context. This repeats the same planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once I already suspected the car, the mark and the repair history just fit what I expected to find. Carman B's 'all clear' almost read to me like it needed double-checking.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant directly describes a prior suspicion shaping interpretation of supporting evidence and discounting a procedurally equivalent clearance. This is the clearest articulation of the planned confirmation-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If Carman B's report had come in first ... I might have closed it out right there. Order mattered more than it should have, probably.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective counterfactual about report order. The hidden manifest contains no primacy-effect instance, and this statement does not establish the defined confirmation-bias mechanism of selectively weighting evidence according to a prior defect hypothesis.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I set the car out and dispatched the rest of the train. Holding the whole consist for one car wasn't going to help anyone ... we'd only eat a partial penalty instead of a full one.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The specification explicitly designates this as a genuine trade-off under competing constraints rather than a biased inference. The participant weighs the unresolved car against the SLA consequences of holding the consist.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If the derailment three weeks earlier had never happened ... I think I isolate just the one car and keep moving.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective counterfactual, not an additional decision-time manifestation. The planned availability instance is mapped to the actual sensor-risk decision and its contemporaneous reasoning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd probably push back harder on the initial time estimate instead of just carrying it forward.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a proposed future correction during retrospective reflection, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd try to look at both carmen's reports side by side instead of one at a time.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a proposed future method for reviewing reports, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: revision of the handed-off 2200/38-car ready-time estimate
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Initial numeric/time estimate from the prior shift's switch list (2200 ready-time, 38 cars) is insufficiently adjusted despite new, materially different information (41 cars, slower retarder cycling in the rain).
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring and adjustment is an established scholarly equivalent of Anchoring Effect, and the finding states the defining insufficient-adjustment mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the handoff target as the initial anchor, the changed car count and retarder speed, and the failure to recalculate the time estimate.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid and directly support the decision-time estimate revision; the stated downstream delay is a reasonable consequence but is not needed for the match.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: response scaling for the borderline GATX 88213 hot-box alert
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The vivid, emotionally salient memory of a recent derailment caused by an overheated bearing disproportionately drives the probability/severity assessment of a borderline, statistically unremarkable hot-box reading, overriding the known false-positive rate of the detector in wet conditions.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is an established scholarly equivalent of Availability Bias, and the finding explicitly describes ease-of-recall overweighting relative to detector frequency.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the vivid recent derailment, the borderline reading, the known wet-weather false-positive history, and the disproportionate escalation to the full cut.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted statements are exact and contemporaneous reasoning evidence; the later clean inspection is correctly treated as counterevidence rather than as the basis for the detection.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: integration of conflicting carman inspection reports for GATX 88213
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: After forming a working hypothesis that the car is defective, the yardmaster selectively weights Carman A's ambiguous mark and an unrelated closed repair-history entry as corroborating evidence, while discounting Carman B's independent clearance that followed the same protocol.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label exactly matches the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the pre-existing suspicion, selective use of Carman A and the old repair note, and discounting of Carman B's procedurally equivalent clearance.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: All quoted evidence is valid and directly supports asymmetric weighting; the report-order counterfactual is included as supporting context but does not create a separate primacy-effect instance.
